learning: If s-bend max_error falls below 0.06 m with steering_oscillation at or under 0.3, turn authority was the limit and the next lever is the geometry. If steering_oscillation rises above 0.32 while max_error does not move, the effective gain is the limit and kp/kd should be retuned rather than the sensors. If the oval finish rate falls below 90%, the narrower track is overshooting on the oval.
notes: Iteration 5 controller kept unchanged with the Builder's wheel_track 0.09 m (from 0.10 m) and the iteration 5 sensor layout, radius 0.040 m and mass 0.5 kg. Only the track changes, so the race isolates turn authority. Results are not yet measured.
rationale: The race evidence favours iteration 5 (mass 0.5 kg, score 422.9). Iteration 6 cut mass to 0.4 kg and scored 422.1: oval finish held at 95%, but s-bend progress fell from 0.72 to 0.59 and s-bend finishes dropped to 2 of 20. So 0.5 kg stays. The remaining s-bend limit is turn authority, not sensing: max_error sits at the 0.06 m off-track limit with about 1.1 line-loss events. The slalom limit is sensor coverage on alternating bends (1.85 line-loss events, progress about 0.14). The Builder's single-variable test narrows wheel_track from 0.10 m to 0.09 m, which raises yaw rate per wheel-speed difference by about 11%. I keep the geometry as the Builder specified: five sensors at y=0.07 m, x = -0.036 to 0.036 in 0.018 m steps, 16 mm footprints, radius 0.040 m, mass 0.5 kg. For the controller, I keep every iteration 5 setting unchanged (kp 3.5, ki 0.05, kd 0.5, base_speed 1.6, weights [-2,-1,0,1,2], last_direction). Scaling kp down by 0.09/0.10 would cancel the extra turn authority the test is meant to measure, so I leave it. The track change is then the only variable against iteration 5. Expected, not measured: s-bend progress above 0.72, s-bend max_error below 0.06 m, and oval finish at or above 90%. The main risk is more steering oscillation, because the effective steering gain rises about 11%.
